title: Add license metadata to pyproject.toml
body:
The pyproject.toml already includes a reference to the license file, but it is helpful to also include the license name directly. This makes it easier to detect the license from package metadata (for a plugin system, say...)

At the moment, ASE shows as "UNKNOWN" to [pip-licenses](https://github.com/stefan6419846/pip-licenses-cli) , which looks a bit bad

```
 alabaster                      1.0.0            BSD License
 asap3                          3.13.6           GNU Lesser General Public License v3 (LGPLv3)
 asciichartpy                   1.5.25           MIT License
 ase                            3.26.0b1         UNKNOWN
 asttokens                      3.0.0            Apache 2.0
 babel                          2.17.0           BSD License
 beautifulsoup4                 4.13.4           MIT License
``` 

This change seems to follow the [current best-practice](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/#license-and-license-files) and gives a nice output with the `pip-licenses` tool linked above.

(Note that it does not work with the original `pip-licenses` because the package [appears unmaintained and does not implement PEP639](https://github.com/raimon49/pip-licenses/issues/225), leading to the fork linked above.)

```
 alabaster                      1.0.0            BSD License
 asap3                          3.13.6           GNU Lesser General Public License v3 (LGPLv3)
 asciichartpy                   1.5.25           MIT License
 ase                            3.26.0b1         LGPL-2.1-or-later
 asttokens                      3.0.0            Apache 2.0
 babel                          2.17.0           BSD License
```

author: ajjackson

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: It would be nice to have the string here, but we have struggled a few times with warnings while building or uploading to pypi (73cecb28ddac48f431ab517080e28fea34ec20a0, 2967d6389c7d46cfed7962468b88780c7a6ca0fc, maybe there are others).  Are you sure pypi likes this string?

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: (Or it might have been twine that didn't like it.  It remains a mystery to me)

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: It has certainly been difficult to keep up with the recommended practice in recent years, it changed a few times. I will try a release with this combination of metadata on a less critical project, and get back to you!

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment raises a concern about whether PyPI will accept the license string, implying the author should verify compatibility or potentially change the value to avoid warnings.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
It looks like twine has taken a while to adopt the new standard, but it should be there in the latest version.

https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-639-round-3-improving-license-clarity-with-better-package-metadata/53020/139

I will test when I get some computer time.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
Ok I have tested with another package, PyPI upload seems good here https://github.com/ajjackson/namedtuple-table/actions/runs/16497001654.

This is on Github using a popular action pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish. v1.12 of the action pins to version 6.1.0 of twine, which supports PEP639

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Thanks for checking.  I approved now.
